before: A file path tells File where to read or write. Use a temporary file for this experiment so you do not overwrite your notes.
File.WriteAllText(path, text) writes the entire text and closes the file. If the file exists, its previous contents are replaced. File.AppendAllText adds text instead.

File operations can fail because of permissions or I/O problems. The try catches failures from its read/write body; finally attempts cleanup. The initial temporary-file creation is before try, and cleanup itself can fail, so those errors are not covered by these catches.

Expected behavior from this example: second when file operations succeed; an environment failure may print the error message instead; cleanup can itself fail. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer: In a disposable folder, compare replacement and appending. Add an explicit newline and explain why the output changes. This is a separate local practice task, not a requirement to mark the reading complete.
after: A file path identifies a file's location. Path.GetTempFileName() creates a temporary file and returns its path. The example uses that file for its work.
File.WriteAllText writes the supplied text and closes the file. If the file already has contents, this method replaces them.
File.ReadAllText reads the contents into a string. Reading back checks what was saved; printing the path alone would only show the location.

File operations can fail. The catches handle read or write failures inside try. finally attempts to delete the temporary file. Creating the file happens before try, and deletion can also fail; these catches do not cover those two steps.
When the file operations succeed, the program prints second. The second write replaces first. Cleanup then deletes the temporary file.
File.AppendAllText adds text after existing contents instead of replacing them. It adds only the supplied text, so a new line appears only if you include one.

before.question: Replace the second WriteAllText with AppendAllText(path, "second"). What does the successful read return?
choices: first followed by an automatic newline and second
before.explanation: Append adds the supplied characters after first. No newline was included, so the result is firstsecond.

after.question: Use AppendAllText(path, "second") for the second write. What does a successful read return?
choices: first and second on separate lines
after.explanation: Appending adds second after first. No new-line character was supplied, so the text is firstsecond.
